title: Add benchmark-lab reporting pipeline v84 and profiling baselines
author: Maya Thompson
description: Motivation: consolidate reporting and profiling improvements for Benchmark Lab v84. This PR wires a new reporting pipeline that aggregates representative-runner outputs, adds profiling baselines for cold-start and steady-state, and introduces a lightweight orchestration shim for running representative workload runners in CI and nightly jobs. Summary: 1) reporting/pipelines/reporting_v84.yaml defines the new pipeline (ingest -> normalize -> metrics-store -> report-gen), 2) benchmark-lab/runners/representative_runners.py adds the runner harness and adapters for Llama/Redwood-backed models, 3) profiling/baselines/runner_config.yaml contains baseline configurations (sequence lengths, batch distributions, warmup policy), 4) docs/benchmark-lab.md documents pipeline usage and migration notes, 5) tests/test_reporting_pipeline.py adds end-to-end smoke tests. Checklist: - [x] Add pipeline YAML and templates - [x] Implement representative runners and config - [x] Add profiling baseline configs and thresholds - [x] Add unit and e2e smoke tests - [x] Update docs and runbook - [x] CI green and merge. Testing notes: ran full benchmark lab unit suite locally and in CI; initial CI run failed due to a race in the runner harness metrics flush (test_reporting_pipeline::test_end_to_end) — fixed by introducing a short flush retry and adding a deterministic flush hook used by tests. Performance verification: included a small profiling run with 500 sample requests across three model variants (gpt-redwood-7b, redwood-alpha-13b, open-llama-13b) to validate baseline percentiles. Backwards compatibility: pipeline is additive; existing v83 jobs unchanged. Rollout: enable v84 as nightlies by default; can be onboarded to PR gating via Linear ticket ENG-4021. Related: ENG-3987 tracks adaptive batching follow-ups. Merge notes: squashed and merged after approvals.
